The top of the Arduino UNO R3 DC barrel jack voltage range is 12 V maximum. The datasheet also notes that VIN can reach 20 V as an absolute maximum rating, which is not recommended for operation.

The Portenta Max Carrier's power jack accepts a maximum input voltage of 36 V (with a minimum of 6 V and typical of 7 V).
The recommended operating conditions table lists the thermal limits minimum as -20 °C (ABX00043 p.6); a separate FCC caution states operation should not be lower than -40 °C (ABX00043 p.25).

The Portenta X8 can source up to 1000 mA maximum from its 3.3 V output, while the Nano RP2040 Connect can source up to 800 mA maximum. Therefore, the Portenta X8 can source more current from its 3.3 V output.

The UNO R4 Minima tolerates a higher DC jack voltage: its VIN input from the VIN pad/DC jack has a maximum of 24 V (minimum 6 V, typical 7.0 V), while the UNO R3's DC barrel jack voltage range has a maximum of 12 V (minimum 7 V).
The Arduino Nano 33 IoT has a maximum VIN rating of 21 V, while the Arduino MKR WiFi 1010 has a maximum VIN rating of 5.5 V; therefore, the Nano 33 IoT has the higher maximum VIN rating.

full.answer: The UNO R4 WiFi runs from a lower minimum VIN: 6 V versus the Mega 2560 Rev3's 7 V.
The UNO R4 Minima's main processor runs at 48 MHz, while the Nano Every's main processor (ATMega4809) runs at up to 20 MHz (maximum). The UNO R4 Minima has the faster main processor clock.
The UNO R3's ATmega328P processor has 32 kB of Flash memory.
The Mega 2560 Rev3's ATmega2560 has 4k bytes of EEPROM.
The MKR WiFi 1010 uses the ATECC508 crypto chip.
The ATSAMD11D14A Arm Cortex-M0+ processor acts as the USB bridge on the Nano Every.
The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 battery charger has a minimum charge current of 512 mA.
No. The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 only supports 3.3 V I/Os and is NOT 5 V tolerant, so directly connecting 5 V signals can damage the board.
The Nicla Sense ME provides 64 KB of SRAM available to the user.
The Nicla Vision uses the GC2145 2 Megapixel CMOS camera sensor.
The Nano RP2040 Connect’s RP2040 microcontroller has 264 kB of on-chip SRAM.
The Arduino GIGA R1 WiFi has 2 analog outputs (DAC), listed as DAC0/DAC1.
The Nano ESP32 is built on the u-blox® NORA-W106-10B radio module, which embeds an ESP32-S3 series SoC and an embedded antenna.
The Portenta C33 is based on the Renesas R7FA6M5BH2CBG microcontroller.
The IOREF pin is connected to 3.3V.
The GIGA R1 WiFi DAC outputs are DAC0 and DAC1, listed on header pins 21 and 22 respectively.
On the MKR WiFi 1010 headers, digital pin D11/SDA carries I2C SDA, and digital pin D12/SCL carries I2C SCL.
On the Arduino Nano Every, I2C SDA is on pin 8, labeled A4/SDA.
On the Nicla Sense ME's J4 battery connector, the battery input pin is called VBAT.
On the Nicla Vision's ESLOV connector (J5), the I2C clock line is pin 3 (SCL).
The VRTC pin on the three-pin header is for the Real Time Clock Battery, and it is used to power the RTC while the board is off.
The UNO R4 Minima has 6 PWM pins: D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, and D11. The pin table also marks D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, and D11 with PWM functions.
